newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel sees no problems clarifying ERM II.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sees no problems clarifying ERM II.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel, following the weekend meeting of European finance ministers in Dublin, said he sees no insurmountable problems clarifying details of the proposed ERM II or the stability pact.
He added that Britain's participation in European economic and monetary union (EMU) would be desirable.
"I see no more insurmountable problems," Waigel said in response to a question at a political party meeting.

Details of the stability pact that remain to be worked out include how sanctions will be imposed for those countries that do not continue to fulfil the convergence criteria after the start of EMU, he said.
Participants must also narrow the definitions of terms such as "exceptional" and "temporary", defining the precise circumstances that would allow a country to acceptably exceed the criteria, he said.

Waigel initially proposed the concept of a stability pact as a means of ensuring that countries which pass the economic test set for entry to the single currency do not later become lax in their fiscal policies.

Over the weekend, officials said a German proposal calling for a deposit of 0.25 percent of GDP for each percentage point of excess deficit was still on the table alongside a European Commission proposal for a smaller deposit per percentage point, capped at a maximum of 0.5 percent.
On Britain's participation in EMU, Waigel said, "I hope that the currency union includes as many stability countries as possible. And the United Kingdom is one of these stability countries."
The financial world is greatly interested that Britain not exclude itself from European integration and EMU, he said.
